scope: Three source-backed desk dossiers; current route conditions and field moments remain unverified.

sources.supports: Designed ramps, benches, walls and multi-sport program.
June 2026 civic programming at Parque 3 de Octubre; not proof of routine skate density.

sources.publisher: Sharif Kahatt / La Residencial San Felipe
sources.supports: Metropolitan monument and traditional-city spatial intent, elevated pedestrian street and mixed-use entries.
Project phases, present visual record and dominant formal viewpoints.
2026 synthesis of resident appropriation, self-determination and visible additions.

contradictions: Published 2019 opening hours are stale and cannot support a route window.
June 2026 civic programming confirms current park use but not routine skate activity, obstacle condition or safe camera position.
composition_questions: Can the obstacle sequence visibly cause a skater's line while waiting and spectating remain architectural rather than incidental?
Which fence, helicopter monument or overlapping rider would sever takeoff from landing?
Does lowering the camera reveal the linked obstacle line more effectively than widening from 50 mm to 35 mm?

source_truth.answer: Municipal sources identify Parque 3 de Octubre as Pueblo Libre's skate plaza with ramps, benches and designed walls for skateboards, BMX, inline skates and scooters.

original_spatial_contract.answer: The park was designed as a sequence of urban obstacles and social edges rather than a single ramp, allowing movement, waiting and spectating to share a civic park.

current_life.answer: Municipal 2026 programs confirm active civic use of the park; daily skate density and current obstacle condition require direct observation.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Ride, push, jump, grind, wait, watch and rest are credible. The strongest relationship links waiting at one edge to a rider's path across two designed obstacles.

architectural_causality.answer: Banks, ledges, walls and benches prescribe approach, launch, landing and pause; the geometry creates both athletic line and social occupation.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Action-only rider images and wide plaza overviews dominate. The underused scene combines rider, waiting group and two linked obstacles without centering the helicopter monument.

light_material_geometry.answer: Low lateral light can separate concrete planes and rider shadow; garúa reduces background clutter but requires enough shutter speed to keep the decisive body geometry.

position_then_optics.answer: Test low beside a ledge, standing oblique across two obstacles and elevated at the social edge. Start 50 mm for relationship; 35 mm only when two devices cannot fit; 85 mm from farther back for layered waiting/action.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Verify current hours and obstacle condition, observe 15 minutes, remain outside rider lines, cap the wait at 25 minutes and avoid identifiable minors without consent.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes if obstacle geometry explains both the rider's motion and the waiting community. A spectacular trick without spatial causality fails.

A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude fence posts and helicopter monument

contradictions: Academic and professional sources establish continued inhabitation but do not verify 2026 access to every elevated passage or current resident tolerance for photography.
composition_questions: Can a resident's everyday route show how monumental density becomes a recognizable street-like neighborhood?
Which tower overlap, parked car or tree mass would erase the elevated-street and plaza hierarchy?
Does stepping onto the diagonal pedestrian axis reveal the contract better than switching to a wider lens?

source_truth.answer: Residencial San Felipe is a phased modern collective-housing complex in Jesús María combining towers, slabs, duplexes, pedestrian systems, commerce and landscaped open space.

original_spatial_contract.answer: It sought metropolitan monumentality while recreating recognizable traditional-city experiences through plazas, elevated pedestrian streets, local commerce and connected entries.

current_life.answer: The complex remains inhabited and its pedestrian plazas, landscape and mixed-use edges remain visible; exact 2026 access and activity cadence require field confirmation.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Walk, enter, shop, greet, sit, play and look out are supported by the designed street/plaza system. The decisive verb is crossing between unlike building types without leaving the pedestrian realm.

architectural_causality.answer: Elevated streets, pilotis, plazas, stairs and landscape buffers connect dissimilar blocks and channel daily movement into shared social space.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Canonical symmetry, tower portraits and green-modernist overviews dominate. A junction where elevated street, ground plaza and present resident route meet is less repeated.

light_material_geometry.answer: Side light articulates pilotis, bridge depth and façade rhythm; overcast protects the green-density relation and allows human gestures to carry contrast.

position_then_optics.answer: Test central plaza at eye level, low under pilotis and oblique from an accessible elevated path. Use 35 mm for section, 50 mm for resident/device relation and 85 mm from distance for old/new urban layering.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Observe ordinary public circulation, avoid dwelling windows and identifiable children, verify elevated-path access, wait 20 minutes for repeated resident movement and leave if challenged.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The image passes when one everyday crossing makes monumental scale and neighborhood intimacy coexist. An empty modernist composition fails inhabitation.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Central plaza diagonal showing tower, slab and connecting path
A_STRUCTURE.expected_action: No event required; three scales must interlock
A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude parked cars and clipped towers

B_HABITAR.position: At junction of plaza, stair and local-use edge
B_HABITAR.expected_action: Resident crosses, greets or carries groceries through designed junction

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Under pilotis looking toward occupied landscape edge
C_ANTI_POSTAL.expected_action: Pedestrian crosses alternating shadow and garden

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: Where pilotis shadow meets mature landscape
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.expected_action: Figure or bicycle crosses shadow boundary
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.edge_guards: Retain structural bay and green buffer

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Oblique position combining elevated street and ground plaza
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.expected_action: Two residents move on different levels toward shared destination
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.fallback: One resident and a visibly occupied local-use threshold

contradictions: The municipal map verifies present identity but not access, conservation or resident activity at a specific prototype.
Published transformations span different prototype houses; no one dwelling may be used as a universal PREVI example.
composition_questions: Can one dwelling show the seed structure and resident-authored addition as a continuous design process rather than before/after damage?
Which signage, vehicle or neighboring prototype would confuse the precise original-versus-added boundary?
Does moving to a party-wall or courtyard angle reveal incremental causality better than compressing façades with 85 mm?

source_truth.answer: PREVI remains an identified Los Olivos urbanization and a documented experimental low-rise/high-density project whose houses were intentionally or effectively transformed by residents.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Seed dwellings, pedestrian axes, plazas, traffic separation and growth capacity were intended to support family evolution within a neighborhood framework.

current_life.answer: Residents have extended façades, fronts, backs and upper levels according to changing needs; current activity at any chosen house must be observed rather than generalized.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Build, extend, repair, enter, sell, converse and appropriate are credible. Meaningful absence can work when additions visibly encode family labor and changing needs.

architectural_causality.answer: Courtyards, party walls, fixed service cores and pedestrian clusters provide the reserve and limits within which residents extend homes.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Aerial masterplans and transformation catalogs dominate. The needed frame isolates one legible seed/addition junction while retaining the shared path or courtyard that makes it urban.

light_material_geometry.answer: Raking light can separate original masonry from later floors, joints and repairs; overcast is safer where color/material differences already carry the chronology.

position_then_optics.answer: Test frontal public path for seed/addition, oblique party-wall view for growth direction and courtyard path for neighborhood relation. Start 50 mm; use 35 mm for shared-space context or 85 mm only for a distant junction.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Remain on public paths, do not photograph into homes, avoid treating adaptation as disorder, verify the specific prototype and observe 20 minutes for a routine threshold action.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes if original growth logic and resident authorship are simultaneously visible without labeling additions as failure. A colorful altered façade alone fails.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Public path oblique to seed house, courtyard and party wall
A_STRUCTURE.expected_action: No person required; growth reserve and shared path read
A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude cars that conceal ground-floor logic
A_STRUCTURE.kill_trigger: Original and addition cannot be distinguished
A_STRUCTURE.access_ethics: Public path; no view into dwelling

B_HABITAR.position: Across a public threshold showing original base and later room
B_HABITAR.expected_action: Resident enters, repairs, opens shop or converses at adapted threshold
B_HABITAR.edge_guards: Keep action tied to the modified device
B_HABITAR.access_ethics: Seek consent for sustained attention; never shoot into home
B_HABITAR.fallback: Meaningful absence through tools, shade and wear

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Ground-level side angle opposing aerial/masterplan cliché
C_ANTI_POSTAL.expected_action: Shared-path use crosses a precise seed/addition seam
C_ANTI_POSTAL.edge_guards: One prototype only; avoid chaotic telephoto stacking

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: At visible masonry/floor addition junction from public edge
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.expected_action: Shadow or routine maintenance gesture crosses construction seam
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.edge_guards: Include load path or courtyard edge

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Oblique public-path view joining seed, addition, threshold and shared route
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.expected_action: Resident uses an added threshold while neighbor crosses original pedestrian path
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.edge_guards: Original, added and communal layers remain distinct
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.kill_trigger: Caption must explain which part grew
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.access_ethics: Consent if a household becomes identifiable
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.fallback: Single threshold action with growth seam and path visible
